chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Jelly Roll Morton as a talker and comedian
summary: Jelly Roll held court on a Harlem corner outside the Rhythm Club and could talk himself into and out of a job.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom

blocks.x: -- because Jelly was just as good a comedian as he was a musician.
Jelly Roll, when he was down at the Rhythm Club at that time down on 132nd Street --
In New York, that's right. And when you'd go down there, like during the summertime, you'd see all

the fellows on the corner, wonder who're them guys talking to -- Jelly had the corner. And Jelly could make some of the funniest statements you ever wanted. We'd work with him. The only man I could see could talk himself into a job and talk himself out of it.
